trail-art: The footprints, drag marks and disturbed plants make this a trail the party can investigate. I keep the later traps and captives out of sight so following the evidence still matters.
snare-art: The exposed rope loop and bent sapling explain the discovered trap. Showing the mechanism without a suspended character keeps the outcome open.
pit-art: The uncovered pit shows its width, depth and camouflaging debris. It is a discovery view; showing a victim or spikes would add consequences and hazards the scene does not establish.
blind-art: The briar screen and two goblin lookouts explain how this position watches the cave approach. The camera shows the position after discovery rather than labeling a hidden ambush on the arrival picture.
kennel-art: Three wolves, their chains and the anchoring stalagmite are the useful details here. Their posture leaves taming, feeding and avoiding them possible rather than assuming an attack.
passage-art: The steep stream passage, wet rock and narrow side route establish the physical challenge. A view from below communicates the climb without exposing rooms farther inside.
overpass-art: The high wooden bridge above the stream explains the vertical relationship. Its sentry belongs to the prepared encounter, while distant passages remain uncertain.
den-art: The ten-foot ledge separates Yeemik's bargaining position from the lower goblins. Sildar belongs to this historical first encounter; the image must not suggest he is still captive after your rescue.
pools-art: Two pools, low stone dams and their feeding waterfall make the flooding mechanism understandable. The prepared guards are shown without depicting the dam being broken or deciding who is swept away.
klarg-art: Klarg, Ripper and two goblins identify the original encounter, with looted crates and a coal fire grounding the room. This is historical encounter art: Klarg's presence must not override his confirmed death.
phandalin-art: A small settlement of modest buildings, dirt streets and older ruined foundations fits frontier Phandalin. The arrival view gives orientation without exposing the Redbrands' underground rooms.
barthen-art: Supplies, tools and ledgers make the delivery destination immediately recognizable. Lean, balding Barthen is approachable; the image does not invent what he knows about Gundren's present condition.
lmop-barthen-exterior: A broad ordinary supply shop gives players a recognizable place to return to at the current checkpoint. Visible goods explain its purpose without promising particular stock or prices.
lmop-stonehill-inn: The modest fieldstone inn provides a public lodging destination. It is not labeled as Gundren's current inn, because your account left that inn unnamed.
lmop-stonehill-common-room: A working hearth, tables and ordinary customers support conversation and rumor gathering. No injured Gundren or announced victory is added to turn an available scene into a confirmed event.
lmop-townmasters-hall: The hall's public frontage and bell distinguish civic business from a tavern or fortress. Notices remain unreadable so the picture cannot invent a posted reward or quest result.
lmop-lionshield-coster: The blue-lion identity and practical weapons distinguish this trading post from Barthen's provisions. Stock is illustrative; the shop record governs availability and prices.
lmop-miners-exchange: Ore samples, scales and business records establish Halia's trade. Her visible professional manner supports negotiation while her affiliations and private motives remain unstated.
lmop-shrine-of-luck: Sister Garaele and a modest stone shrine fit a small frontier religious site. Invented clover heraldry was removed; the picture supplies a meeting place without revealing her private mission.
lmop-alderleaf-farm: An ordinary farm and halfling household make hospitality plausible. The image does not expose Carp's secret route or decide whether the family shares it.
lmop-sleeping-giant: A rough roadside tap house expresses the establishment's reputation without turning it into a palace. The confrontation remains a separately staged encounter.
lmop-sleeping-giant-interior: Grista's worn common room gives a usable conversation setting. Its rough furniture and cramped tables suggest atmosphere without forcing violence or adding a secret headquarters.
lmop-edermath-orchard: The orchard and older half-elf make Daran's quieter life visible. His history and the information he may offer stay in the NPC card rather than becoming obvious heraldry.
lmop-redbrand-confrontation: Four scarlet-cloaked ruffians establish the prepared street challenge. Their confrontational stance sets pressure but does not show a player being hit or choose how the party responds.
lmop-tresendar-manor: A ruined hilltop residence establishes the entrance context. Its damaged domestic architecture avoids implying that the party faces an intact occupied fortress.
lmop-tresendar-tunnel: The hillside opening provides a discovered alternate approach. The view stops at the entrance so players do not gain a free overview of the hideout.
lmop-ruffian-barracks: Two double bunks, stored provisions and three ruffians describe a small lived-in guard room. Plain scarlet garments identify the gang without invented dragon crests.
lmop-armory: Weapon racks, quivers and scarlet cloaks establish a usable supply room. Individual stock totals remain in the room card; perspective artwork is not a reliable inventory count.
lmop-redbrand-storeroom: Crates, barrels and a rough transition into the cavern distinguish storage from a ceremonial chamber. Secret doors and hidden contents are omitted until searched.
lmop-bugbear-barracks: Three bugbears, Mosk's eye patch and Droop distinguish this encounter from another ruffian room. Droop's presence allows rescue or conversation without deciding his relationship with the party.
lmop-common-room: Four ruffians gambling around a table make the social interruption readable. Kegs and plain cloth support the source's common-room function; invented gang emblems were removed.
lmop-triboar-trail: A modest overland trail through foothills provides travel context. Distant terrain is atmosphere rather than a measured route or a newly discovered destination.
lmop-conyberry: Ruined homes and overgrown streets show an abandoned settlement. The picture does not add surviving residents or advertise Agatha's exact hiding place.
lmop-agathas-lair: Woven branches and old elven household objects express a shelter with a former inhabitant. Keeping Agatha absent preserves the moment before her appearance.
lmop-agatha-reveal: A spectral elven woman within the same woven shelter makes the encounter's identity clear. A composed pose supports a difficult conversation rather than assuming combat.
lmop-stirge-encounter: Flying stirges approaching an ordinary camp establish the threat. The artwork leaves attacks, damage and the encounter's eventual numbers to the encounter card.
lmop-ghoul-encounter: Ghouls approaching camp make the nighttime danger visible. No player victim is included, and the image remains a reusable wilderness encounter rather than a recorded attack.
lmop-ogre-encounter: A large solitary ogre on the route communicates scale and an obstacle. The open surroundings allow avoidance or negotiation as well as a fight.
lmop-goblin-encounter: Small goblins using roadside vegetation fit an ambush threat. The image shows discovered opponents without assigning their targets or the party's response.
lmop-hobgoblin-encounter: Organized armored travelers distinguish hobgoblins from goblins. The route remains ordinary terrain so the image does not invent a fort or faction headquarters.
lmop-orc-encounter: Orcs among rocky foothills provide a separate optional wilderness encounter. This is not the cleared Wyvern Tor camp and does not undo that success.
lmop-wolf-encounter: Wolves on a wooded route provide a believable animal encounter. Their alert posture leaves space for feeding, avoidance or retreat without illustrating an attack result.
lmop-owlbear-encounter: A feathered bear-bodied creature makes the owlbear recognizable. The woodland route supplies context without inventing a nest, treasure or captured person.
lmop-thundertree-approach: Roofless buildings, vegetation and the distant tower give orientation to the abandoned village. Hidden creatures remain absent until their individual encounters are staged.
lmop-blighted-cottages: Two overgrown damaged cottages fit the location's modest scale. Blights blend into the vegetation rather than being displayed before discovery.
lmop-brown-horse: The faded horse sign, damaged taproom and abandoned furnishings identify the old tavern. Inert remains and empty spaces preserve the moment before any undead stir.
lmop-druids-watch: A comparatively intact cottage contrasts with surrounding ruins and provides a plausible refuge. The view does not announce Reidoth's knowledge or promise that he will help.
lmop-blighted-farmhouse: A small ruined farmhouse overtaken by plants fits the village's decline. Concealed blights are omitted so approaching it still involves uncertainty.
lmop-ruined-store: A damaged storefront, broken roof and webs hint at danger without naming every inhabitant. Hidden valuables remain out of sight.
lmop-spider-reveal: Two giant spiders become visible only in the reveal view. The same ruined shop supplies their terrain rather than moving them into a generic enormous spider cavern.
lmop-old-smithy: A forge, anvil and collapsed workshop roof identify the building's former use. Undead are not shown attacking before the encounter starts.
lmop-herbalists-shop: Shelves, containers and creeping vegetation establish the old herbalist's premises. Hidden jewelry is not presented as obvious treasure.
lmop-town-square: The weathered statue and open square give the village a recognizable public landmark. Nearby threats stay separate from the orientation view.
lmop-old-garrison: Beds and military remnants establish a former guard building. Motionless remains do not prematurely reveal their animation or decide the fight.
lmop-weavers-cottage: The ruined domestic workshop gives this room its ordinary former purpose. It remains a small cottage rather than an invented magical shrine.
lmop-cultist-cottage: An intact-looking cottage provides the initial exterior before meeting its occupants. No black-dragon symbol advertises their hidden allegiance from outside.
lmop-cultists-reveal: Six cloaked adults with dragon masks establish the revealed cult group. An ordinary cottage meeting leaves negotiation possible; no invented altar or sacrifice is added.
lmop-castle-approach: Unequal damaged towers surrounded by woodland establish Cragmaw's recognizable silhouette. The picture cannot supply the route here before the players learn it.
lmop-castle-entrance: The raised approach and damaged gates show the main entry clearly. Hidden defenders and alternate entrances stay outside this first view.
lmop-trapped-hall: An apparently usable dusty hall preserves the hidden hazard. The image does not mark a trigger or show collapse before detection.
lmop-hall-collapse: Fallen masonry and timbers explain the triggered change to the hall. No trapped player or predetermined injury is illustrated.
lmop-archer-post: Two goblin archers beside a narrow opening explain the defensive position. Their sightline is more useful than a generic goblin portrait.
lmop-ruined-barracks: Damaged walls, crude bedding and goblin occupants show an improvised barracks. The room remains visibly part of a ruined castle.
lmop-castle-storeroom: Stored food, equipment and neglected supplies establish ordinary logistics. Recoverable items are not highlighted as if the party has already claimed them.
lmop-hobgoblin-barracks: Four hobgoblins and simple sleeping arrangements establish organized occupation. Their visible equipment supports the encounter without deciding their orders or reaction.
lmop-banquet-hall: Two long tables and a tall damaged hall fit the castle's former dining space. Yegg and the goblin group occupy it without an invented royal feast.
lmop-dark-hall: Old devotional statues and curtains establish a repurposed sacred room. The grick remains concealed in this neutral view.
lmop-grick-reveal: The grick is revealed above the same devotional architecture. Its perched position explains the danger without announcing hidden treasure.
lmop-goblin-shrine: Three robed goblins and a black-covered altar show the shrine's present use. Visible ritual objects support the room description without revealing concealed loot.
lmop-postern-gate: A smaller reinforced side entrance provides an alternate approach. It is a discovered access point, not a guarantee that it is unlocked or safe.
lmop-ruined-tower: Collapsed masonry and overgrowth explain the damaged tower and possible access. The concealed doorway is not outlined for players before discovery.
lmop-guard-barracks: Two guards, bedding and a brazier make the active defensive position understandable. The barred entrance remains a practical obstacle rather than a cinematic prison scene.
lmop-owlbear-tower: A large owlbear in a dark tall tower fits the confined encounter. Hidden treasure remains above or outside the view, and the creature's presence is staged after discovery.
lmop-old-entrance: Carved dwarf and gnome figures, old battle remains and a spacious entrance hall establish the mine's past. Stirges remain concealed until the encounter reveals them.
lmop-assayers-office: A counter, balances and document cubbies make the old accounting office distinct. The strongbox stays closed; its contents are a search result, not free visual information.
lmop-south-barracks: Stone bunks and a cold brazier preserve the old mine's construction. Three ghouls identify the prepared encounter without adding a larger horde.
lmop-ruined-storeroom: Old containers, secure northern storage and an eastern collapse explain the room's condition. It is useful exploration terrain, not an invented treasure vault.
lmop-fungi-cavern: Tall luminous fungi establish unusual growth and the route's environmental difficulty. A neutral view avoids announcing the poisonous response before disturbance.
lmop-fungal-gas: Spores spreading from the same growth show the triggered environmental hazard. No injured character or guaranteed saving-throw failure is pictured.
lmop-great-cavern: The lower dining space, tables, cold braziers and side ledges communicate a large room with meaningful elevation. Concealed ghouls remain absent from the first view.
lmop-dark-pool: A dark pool, mussels, steps and the incoming stream give observable clues and routes. The submerged skeleton and valuable rings remain hidden.
lmop-wizards-quarters: Scorched furniture, books and an iron chest establish damaged guest quarters. Mormesk is absent until his appearance, and the closed chest does not disclose its contents.
lmop-mormesk-reveal: A spectral former wizard appears in the same burned quarters. His presence supports a conversation or confrontation without deciding what agreement the party reaches.
lmop-booming-cavern: Water surging against stone ledges explains the sound that gives Wave Echo Cave its name. The view makes the vertical waterfront clear without adding a ship or artificial harbor.
